labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Feature Description
The Workspace → Tasks view does not appear to offer a way to switch which Kanban board it is showing.

The Kanban system already supports multiple boards via the CLI and env/config (`hermes kanban boards switch`, `--board <slug>`, `HERMES_KANBAN_BOARD`), but the Workspace UI seems to have no equivalent control.

## Motivation
If I am using Workspace as the main place to inspect tasks, I should be able to switch boards there instead of bouncing out to the CLI or editing env/state by hand.

## Proposed Solution
Add a visible board selector in the Workspace Tasks section, or a board switcher in the surrounding Workspace navigation, that lets the user pick the active board.

items.title: fix(bedrock): static context window table reports 200K for Claude 4.x models (should be 1M)
items.body:
## Bug

The static fallback table `BEDROCK_CONTEXT_LENGTHS` in `agent/bedrock_adapter.py` hardcodes all Claude models at 200,000 tokens. However, per [AWS Bedrock documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-anthropic-claude-sonnet-4-6.html), Claude 4.x models (Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5, Opus 4.5, Opus 4.1) all have a **1M token context window** on Bedrock.

This causes hermes to compress/truncate context much earlier than necessary when using Bedrock as a provider.

## Affected code

```python
# agent/bedrock_adapter.py line ~1233
BEDROCK_CONTEXT_LENGTHS: Dict[str, int] = {
    "anthropic.claude-opus-4-6":     200_000,   # should be 1_000_000
    "anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6":   200_000,   # should be 1_000_000
    "anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5":   200_000,   # should be 1_000_000
    "anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5":    200_000,   # should be 1_000_000
    ...
}
```

## Expected behavior

Claude 4.x models on Bedrock should report a 1M context window, matching the AWS documentation. Only Claude 3.x and the original Claude 4.0 (Sonnet 4, Opus 4) should remain at 200K.

## Environment

- hermes-agent v0.15.1 (commit 4f7fe9bcf)
- Provider: AWS Bedrock (us-east-1)
- Models affected: all `anthropic.claude-*-4-*` entries

items.title: [Kanban] Align dashboard columns with scheduled/review statuses
items.body:
## Intent
Align the Kanban dashboard frontend status columns with the backend's canonical board columns so scheduled/review tasks are visible instead of being hidden or mis-bucketed.

## Context
The Kanban dashboard backend already treats these statuses as first-class board columns:

- `plugins/kanban/dashboard/plugin_api.py`: `BOARD_COLUMNS = ["triage", "todo", "scheduled", "ready", "running", "blocked", "review", "done"]`
- `/api/plugins/kanban/board` returns columns based on that backend list.

The dashboard frontend bundle still has:

- `plugins/kanban/dashboard/dist/index.js`: `const COLUMN_ORDER = ["triage", "todo", "ready", "running", "blocked", "done"]`

That omits `scheduled` and `review`, which makes the UI projection drift from Kanban runtime truth. The `review` lane is especially important for implementation → review/Warden-style gates; `scheduled` is important for delayed/follow-up cards.

## Requirements
- [ ] Add `scheduled` and `review` to the frontend visible column order.
- [ ] Ensure column labels, descriptions/help text, move/drag/drop, and any status menus support both statuses.
- [ ] Keep the frontend order exactly aligned with backend `BOARD_COLUMNS`, excluding only statuses that are intentionally not visible such as `archived`.
- [ ] Ensure client-side filtering/searching does not drop tasks in `scheduled` or `review`.
- [ ] Preserve existing board selection, tenant filtering, assignee filtering, and live update behavior.

## Non-goals
- Do not add new statuses.
- Do not change Kanban database schema.
- Do not implement the full Executor Board worker panel in this issue; that should be a separate feature issue.
- Do not expose archived tasks as a normal visible column unless already supported by existing archived UI behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: A task with `status='scheduled'` appears in a visible Scheduled column in the dashboard.
- [ ] AC2: A task with `status='review'` appears in a visible Review column in the dashboard.
- [ ] AC3: Drag/drop or status-change controls can move tasks into and out of `scheduled` and `review` without validation errors.
- [ ] AC4: Search, tenant filter, and assignee filter continue to include matching `scheduled`/`review` tasks.
- [ ] AC5: Tests cover the frontend column order/status support; existing Kanban dashboard backend tests continue to pass.
- [ ] AC6: i18n fallback strings exist for Scheduled/Review labels and any relevant confirmation/help text.

## Evidence / References
- Backend canonical columns: `plugins/kanban/dashboard/plugin_api.py`, around `BOARD_COLUMNS`.
- Frontend drift: `plugins/kanban/dashboard/dist/index.js`, `COLUMN_ORDER` currently omits `scheduled` and `review`.
- Backend tests already assert scheduled/review column behavior through `/api/plugins/kanban/board`.

## Open Questions
- [ ] If there is an uncommitted source file or build pipeline for the dashboard bundle, should this change update source + generated bundle or only the checked-in bundle?

## Decisions
- 2026-06-02: Treat Kanban backend/runtime status as source of truth; frontend must project all first-class board columns.

items.title: [Kanban] Add Executor Board active worker panel
items.body:
## Intent
Add an Executor Board / active-worker panel to the Kanban dashboard so operators can see not only which tasks are `running`, but which worker processes are actually alive, what they are executing, and whether they are healthy or stale.

## Context
The Kanban dashboard backend already exposes most of the raw data needed for an executor-level view:

- `GET /api/plugins/kanban/workers/active` — active `task_runs` rows with task/run/profile/PID/heartbeat context.
- `GET /api/plugins/kanban/runs/{run_id}/inspect` — live PID stats via psutil when available.
- `GET /api/plugins/kanban/tasks/{task_id}/log?tail=...` — bounded worker log tail.
- `GET /api/plugins/kanban/diagnostics` and per-task diagnostics — stale/desync warnings.
- Existing task drawer/recovery actions already expose task details, comments, run history, reclaim/reassign/decompose-style operations.

The current board view is task-state oriented. For multi-agent operations, operators need a process/runtime projection that answers:

- Which workers are alive right now?
- Which profile/assignee/run/PID/workspace is attached to each task?
- Is the PID alive, stale, over max runtime, missing heartbeat, or otherwise suspicious?
- What is the latest bounded log tail?
- Is Kanban state desynchronized from runtime state?

## Requirements
- [ ] Add an "Executor Board" or "Active Workers" panel/section in the Kanban dashboard.
- [ ] Fetch and render `GET /api/plugins/kanban/workers/active` for the selected board.
- [ ] Each worker card/row shows at minimum: task id, task title, assignee/profile, run_id, worker_pid, started age, last heartbeat age, max runtime, claim/lock context when useful, and a link/action to open the task drawer.
- [ ] For each active run, surface live inspection from `GET /api/plugins/kanban/runs/{run_id}/inspect` or a clear unavailable state when psutil/process data is unavailable.
- [ ] Show bounded log tail from `GET /api/plugins/kanban/tasks/{task_id}/log?tail=...` behind an expandable/details action, not as always-loaded unbounded text.
- [ ] Surface diagnostics badges/warnings for stale heartbeat, missing PID, dead PID while task is running, or other existing diagnostic rules.
- [ ] Keep secrets and raw prompts/env out of the panel. Do not display unbounded full logs by default.
- [ ] Preserve existing board filters and selected-board semantics.
- [ ] Provide loading, empty, and error states.

## Non-goals
- Do not add worker mutation controls beyond existing safe recovery actions unless already available in the dashboard.
- Do not change Kanban DB schema unless strictly necessary.
- Do not implement GitHub Issue/PR truth projection in this issue; that should remain a separate ops projection feature.
- Do not expose the dashboard as a public unauthenticated ops surface.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: When at least one `task_runs` row is active with a live `worker_pid`, the dashboard shows it in an Active Workers/Executor panel.
- [ ] AC2: Worker entries include task id/title, assignee/profile, run_id, PID, started age, heartbeat age, max runtime, and task drawer link/action.
- [ ] AC3: The panel indicates whether live inspection reports the process as alive, dead, access-denied, or unavailable because psutil is missing.
- [ ] AC4: A bounded log-tail view is available per worker and respects a safe tail limit.
- [ ] AC5: Existing diagnostics are reflected as visible badges/warnings without blocking normal board rendering.
- [ ] AC6: Empty state clearly says no active workers for the selected board.
- [ ] AC7: Tests cover API integration/rendering for active workers, inspect unavailable/dead/alive states where practical, and log-tail display behavior.
- [ ] AC8: Existing Kanban dashboard tests continue to pass.

## Evidence / References
- Backend active worker API: `plugins/kanban/dashboard/plugin_api.py`, `@router.get("/workers/active")`.
- Backend run inspect API: `plugins/kanban/dashboard/plugin_api.py`, `@router.get("/runs/{run_id}/inspect")`.
- Backend task log API: `plugins/kanban/dashboard/plugin_api.py`, `@router.get("/tasks/{task_id}/log")`.
- Current frontend bundle: `plugins/kanban/dashboard/dist/index.js` does not appear to call `workers/active` or render an Active Workers panel.

## Open Questions
- [ ] Should the panel live above the board columns, in a side rail, or as a collapsible tab? Default recommendation: collapsed/compact strip above columns, expanding into worker cards.
- [ ] Should inspection polling use the existing board live-update cadence or a separate slower interval? Default recommendation: separate conservative interval to avoid excessive psutil/log calls.

## Decisions
- 2026-06-02: Treat Kanban task state and executor/process state as separate projections; dashboard should expose both so operators can diagnose runtime desync quickly.

items.title: [QQ Bot] Exception in _reconnect() bypasses backoff counter, causing max reconnect loop

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Bug

When `QQBotAdapter._reconnect()` raises an exception (e.g. DNS resolution failure on a stale DNS cache), the exception propagates up and the backoff counter is never incremented. The caller retries immediately, hitting the same error again.

## Root Cause
`_reconnect()` is called directly without a `try/except` wrapper, so exceptions are unhandled at the call site.

## Fix
Wrap the `_reconnect()` call in `try/except Exception` and increment the backoff counter on any exception:
```python
try:
    if await self._reconnect(backoff_idx):
        backoff_idx = 0
        quick_disconnect_count = 0
    else:
        backoff_idx += 1
except Exception:
    backoff_idx += 1
    if backoff_idx >= MAX_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS:
        logger.error("[%s] Max reconnect attempts reached", self._log_tag)
        self._status = "failed"
        return False
```

## Environment
- Hermes QQ Bot adapter
- Hermes version: 0.15.x

items.title: [Bug]: SSH backend crashes on non-UTF8 subprocess output during _ensure_remote_dirs
items.body:
### Bug Description

The Hermes Agent SSH terminal backend can fail to initialize if an internal SSH subprocess emits non-UTF8 bytes on stdout or stderr.

The crash occurs before the user command runs, during `_SSHEnvironment._ensure_remote_dirs()`.

The problematic pattern is the use of `subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True, text=True, ...)` without `errors="replace"` or another tolerant decoding strategy.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Hermes with the SSH terminal backend:

```env
   TERMINAL_ENV=ssh
   TERMINAL_SSH_HOST=<host>
   TERMINAL_SSH_USER=<user>
   TERMINAL_SSH_KEY=<key>
```
2. Point it at a Windows OpenSSH target using Git Bash/MSYS as the remote shell.

3. Restart Hermes gateway:
  
```bash
   hermes --profile <profile> gateway restart
```

4. Run any Hermes terminal/file/search tool that initializes the SSH backend.

5. Hermes fails before executing the requested command with:
   
```text
   UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x83 in position 0: invalid start byte
```
   
6. Traceback points to:

```text
   /usr/local/lib/hermes-agent/tools/environments/ssh.py", line 137, in _ensure_remote_dirs
       subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
```   
7. Manual SSH using the same host/user/key works:
   
```bash
   ssh <host> 'bash -lc "echo ok; whoami; pwd; mkdir -p ~/.hermes/tmp && echo made-dir"'
``` 
   and returns successfully, showing the failure is specific to Hermes’s strict decoding of SSH subprocess output.

### Expected Behavior

Hermes should not crash the SSH backend because of undecodable subprocess output.

It should either:

- decode with `errors="replace"`;
- capture bytes and decode explicitly with fallback handling;
- or surface the remote stderr/stdout safely in the tool error response.

A non-UTF8 byte in SSH output should not prevent backend initialization.

### Actual Behavior

Terminal/file/search tools fail before executing the requested command.

Example traceback:
```text
Failed to execute command: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x83 in position 0: invalid start byte

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/lib/hermes-agent/tools/terminal_tool.py", line 1938, in terminal_tool
    new_env = _create_environment(
              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/hermes-agent/tools/terminal_tool.py", line 1278, in _create_environment
    return _SSHEnvironment(
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/hermes-agent/tools/environments/ssh.py", line 71, in init
    self._ensure_remote_dirs()
  File "/usr/local/lib/hermes-agent/tools/environments/ssh.py", line 137, in _ensure_remote_dirs
    subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
  File ".../python3.11/subprocess.py", line 550, in run
    stdout, stderr = process.communicate(input, timeout=timeout)
  File ".../python3.11/subprocess.py", line 1209, in communicate
    stdout, stderr = self._communicate(input, endtime, timeout)
  File ".../python3.11/subprocess.py", line 2157, in _communicate
    stderr = self._translate_newlines(stderr,
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".../python3.11/subprocess.py", line 1086, in _translate_newlines
    data = data.decode(encoding, errors)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x83 in position 0: invalid start byte
```

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Discord

### Debug Report

```shell
Report       https://paste.rs/XFdjK
  agent.log    https://paste.rs/vxTV0
  gateway.log  https://paste.rs/NKEv7
```

### Operating System

Linux/aarch64, Windows 11

### Python Version

Python 3.11.15

### Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.15.1 (2026.5.29)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The SSH backend captures output from internal SSH setup commands using Python `subprocess.run(..., text=True)` without specifying a tolerant decode error handler.

In Python, `text=True` decodes `stdout` and `stderr` using the process locale/default encoding with strict error handling. If the SSH process emits any byte sequence that is not valid UTF-8, `subprocess.run()` raises `UnicodeDecodeError` while translating captured output.

This happens before Hermes gets a chance to inspect the subprocess result or report the actual SSH stderr/stdout.

In this case, the crash occurs during SSH backend initialization:
```text
/usr/local/lib/hermes-agent/tools/environments/ssh.py", line 137, in _ensure_remote_dirs
    subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
The same strict-decoding pattern appears in multiple SSH backend calls:
text
104: subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15)
116: subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
137: subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
177: subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
269: subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
```
Because these calls are part of SSH environment initialization, a single undecodable byte in SSH output can prevent all terminal/file/search tools from starting, even when the underlying SSH connection and remote command execution are working.

Manual SSH to the same host/user/key succeeds, so the failure is not necessarily authentication or SSH connectivity. It is Hermes’s strict decoding of captured SSH subprocess output.


### Proposed Fix (optional)

Decode SSH subprocess output defensively.

The simplest fix is to add `errors="replace"` to the affected `subprocess.run()` calls:
```python
subprocess.run(
    cmd,
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    errors="replace",
    timeout=10,
)
```
For example, change `_ensure_remote_dirs()` from:
```python
def _ensure_remote_dirs(self) -> None:
    """Create base ~/.hermes directory tree on remote in one SSH call."""
    base = f"{self._remote_home}/.hermes"
    dirs = [base, f"{base}/skills", f"{base}/credentials", f"{base}/cache"]
    cmd = self._build_ssh_command()
    cmd.append(quoted_mkdir_command(dirs))
    subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
```
to:
```python
def _ensure_remote_dirs(self) -> None:
    """Create base ~/.hermes directory tree on remote in one SSH call."""
    base = f"{self._remote_home}/.hermes"
    dirs = [base, f"{base}/skills", f"{base}/credentials", f"{base}/cache"]
    cmd = self._build_ssh_command()
    cmd.append(quoted_mkdir_command(dirs))
    subprocess.run(
        cmd,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        errors="replace",
        timeout=10,
    )
```
This prevents undecodable bytes from crashing environment initialization. Invalid byte sequences would be represented as replacement characters instead of raising `UnicodeDecodeError`.

A more explicit alternative is to capture bytes and decode manually:
```python
result = subprocess.run(
    cmd,
    capture_output=True,
    text=False,
    timeout=10,
)

stdout = result.stdout.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
stderr = result.stderr.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
```
That approach may be preferable if Hermes wants consistent UTF-8 handling regardless of system locale.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: fix(discord): clarify button shows Python repr of dict choices + mid-word truncation
items.body:
## Bug

The Discord adapter's `clarify` button render shows raw Python repr when the LLM emits dict-typed choices instead of bare strings. Long choices are also truncated mid-word with no margin for the `1. ` prefix and the `...` ellipsis.

## Visual symptom

![Screenshot_2026-06-02-06-47-43-87_572064f74bd5f9fa804b05334aa4f912.jpg](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c8021d19-dae0-4226-8b4e-e3e295e63372)



A button on the user's screen reads:
```
1. {'description': 'Tight, well-illustrated, covers all 3...
```
instead of the intended:
```
1. Tight, well-illustrated, covers all 3 audiences (patients, families,…)
```

## Root cause

`plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py:4192-4194` (in `send_clarify`):

```python
clean_choices = [
    str(c).strip() for c in (choices or []) if c is not None and str(c).strip()
]
```

When `c` is a dict, `str(c)` produces the Python repr of the dict — including the field names and braces — which is then passed verbatim to `discord.ui.Button(label=...)`. The user sees a debug-style dump on the button instead of the choice text.

This is a known failure mode for several LLM providers and tool-call parsers: when the schema declares `choices: array of string`, the model sometimes emits `choices: array of {description: string}` instead, matching a related shape it has seen in other tool calls. The current code happily coerces the dict to a string and hides the malformed call, producing garbage on screen.

The same pattern exists in `tools/clarify_tool.py:51` (the tool itself), but in the `clarify_tool` case the model emits strings consistently and the bug is masked. On the Discord adapter boundary, the malformed payload reaches the user.

A secondary issue: `ClarifyChoiceView` (line ~5591 in the same file) caps labels at 75 chars + `...`, leaving no margin for the `1. ` prefix. Long choices get cut mid-word (`"covers all 3..."`) and waste 2 chars on the three-dot ellipsis.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run Hermes gateway with the Discord platform connected.
2. Send a message that triggers the `clarify` tool with multiple choices.
3. The model emits a malformed tool call: `choices=[{"description": "Tight, well-illustrated, covers all 3 audiences (patients, families, curious general readers)"}, "Balanced, ~30 pages, the default", "Comprehensive, 40+ pages, no topic skipped"]`
4. Observe: button 0 reads `1. {'description': 'Tight, well-illustrated, covers all 3...` and the trailing portion of the description is missing.

## Expected behavior

`1. Tight, well-illustrated, covers all 3 audiences (patients, families,…` — the dict unwrapped, the full intent visible, the cut at a word boundary.

## Proposed fix

PR forthcoming on a feature branch. Two changes:

1. Replace the `str(c).strip()` coercion with a `_flatten_choice()` helper that unwraps the common LLM-emitted dict shapes (`label`, `description`, `text`, `title`, `name`, `value`) before stringifying. Strings pass through unchanged; dicts without any string value are dropped instead of leaking a Python repr onto the user's screen.

2. Tighten `ClarifyChoiceView` label truncation: respect the 80-char Discord hard limit, cut at the last word boundary when possible, use a single U+2026 ellipsis to reclaim 2 chars of budget.

Test coverage will grow from 14 → 16 in `tests/gateway/test_discord_clarify_buttons.py` (added `test_unwraps_dict_choices_to_description` and `test_truncates_long_choice_label_breaks_on_word_boundary`).

## Impact

- Affects every Discord user who triggers `clarify` with multi-choice options on a model that emits dict-typed choices.
- Other platforms (Telegram, Mattermost, Feishu, etc.) are likely affected by the same dict-unwrap pattern but use different render code paths — those will be addressed in follow-up PRs.
- No data loss, no security issue, no API breakage.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: `main` @ `85b65e29f`
- Discord adapter: `plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py`
- Reproduced on Discord mobile (iOS), confirmed also affects desktop.

items.title: TUI branding shows all MCP servers as "failed" due to race condition with background discovery

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

The TUI branding screen displays all configured MCP servers as red "failed" immediately after startup, even though the servers are actually connected and fully functional. The status never self-corrects — it persists until the user manually runs `/reload-mcp`.

## Root Cause

There is a race condition between the TUI's session creation and the background MCP discovery thread:

1. **TUI starts** → `tui_gateway/entry.py` spawns a background `tui-mcp-discovery` thread (line 255-260) that calls `discover_mcp_tools()`
2. **TUI creates a session** → gateway calls `_session_info()` → `get_mcp_status()` (line 1601)
3. **At this point**, the background discovery thread hasn't completed yet, so the `_servers` dict in `tools/mcp_tool.py` is empty
4. `get_mcp_status()` returns `connected: False` for all configured servers (line 3564-3569)
5. **`session.info` event is emitted** to the TUI with stale MCP status
6. **TUI branding renders** → `branding.tsx` line 258 shows `<Text color={t.color.error}>failed</Text>`
7. **MCP discovery completes** → `_servers` is now populated with all servers connected
8. **But `session.info` is never re-emitted** — the branding screen keeps showing the stale "failed" status

## Code Paths

**TUI branding display** (`ui-tui/src/components/branding.tsx` line 248-262):
```tsx
{(info.mcp_servers ?? []).map(s => (
  <Text key={s.name}>
    <Text color={t.color.muted}>{`  ${s.name} `}</Text>
    <Text color={t.color.muted}>: </Text>
    {s.connected ? (
      <Text color={t.color.text}>{s.tools} tool{s.tools === 1 ? '' : 's'}</Text>
    ) : (
      <Text color={t.color.error}>failed</Text>
    )}
  </Text>
))}
```

**MCP status check** (`tools/mcp_tool.py` line 3550-3569):
```python
for name, cfg in configured.items():
    server = active_servers.get(name)
    if server and server.session is not None:
        entry = {"connected": True, ...}
    else:
        entry = {"connected": False, ...}  # <-- hits this when discovery not done
```

**Background discovery** (`tui_gateway/entry.py` line 245-260):
```python
def _discover_mcp_background() -> None:
    from tools.mcp_tool import discover_mcp_tools
    discover_mcp_tools()

_mcp_thread = threading.Thread(target=_discover_mcp_background, name="tui-mcp-discovery", daemon=True)
_mcp_thread.start()
```

**Session info emission** (`tui_gateway/server.py` line 590-595):
```python
info = _session_info(agent, current)  # calls get_mcp_status() — too early!
_emit("session.info", sid, info)
```

## Evidence

- `hermes mcp test` confirms all 5 servers are actually connected (all ✓ Connected)
- `agent.log` shows `MCP: registered 78 tool(s) from 5 server(s)` — all successful
- TUI branding persists showing red "failed" indefinitely
- Running `/reload-mcp` fixes the display (it calls `discover_mcp_tools()` synchronously then re-emits `session.info`)

## Suggested Fix

Either:
1. **Emit `session.info` after MCP discovery completes** — in the background discovery thread, after `discover_mcp_tools()` returns, emit a fresh `session.info` event
2. **Wait for discovery before first session** — block session creation briefly (with timeout) until the `tui-mcp-discovery` thread signals completion
3. **Have the TUI poll** — the branding component could periodically re-fetch MCP status

Option 1 is the simplest and least disruptive.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: latest main branch
- macOS 14.8.7, Python 3.11
- 5 MCP servers configured (fetch, filesystem, github, intellij, time)
- TUI mode (`hermes --tui` or `hermes`)

items.title: [Bug]: inconsistent naming in kanban dashboard interface

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
## Bug

When repairing/normalising tool-call names, duplicated `mcp_` prefixes (e.g. `mcp_mcp_<server>_<tool>` or otherwise doubled namespace prefixes) are not collapsed before the fuzzy tool-name match runs. The doubled prefix throws off the fuzzy matcher so a valid tool name fails to resolve.

## Impact

Tool calls that should resolve cleanly are dropped or mis-resolved, causing the agent to retry or fail a step that references an otherwise-valid MCP tool.

## Expected

Duplicated `mcp_` / namespace prefixes should be normalised (collapsed to a single prefix) before fuzzy matching, so the canonical tool name resolves.

## Fix

Normalise duplicated `mcp_` prefixes prior to the fuzzy match (see PR #33359), with a regression test in `tests/run_agent/test_repair_tool_call_name.py`.

Platform observed: Linux (Ubuntu, CT133 container, kernel 6.8.12).

items.title: 【Bug】Dashboard WebSocket frontend missing status_callback — lifecycle events not delivered to web clients

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
### Summary

The Hermes Dashboard (WebSocket-based web UI) does not register a `status_callback` on the agent, so all lifecycle/status events emitted via `_emit_status()` are lost for WebSocket clients. These events reach CLI users (via `_vprint`) and messaging gateway platforms (Telegram/Discord via `status_callback`), but not the Dashboard frontend.

### Affected Events

All `_emit_status()` and `_emit_warning()` calls are invisible to Dashboard users:

- **Iteration budget exhausted**: `⚠️ Iteration budget exhausted (45/45) — asking model to summarise`
- **Context compression**: `⚠️ Compacting context...` / compression done
- **Model fallback**: `🔄 Primary model failed — switching to fallback: ...`
- **Memory flush**: Memory flush warnings
- **Auxiliary compression**: Compression timeout/fallback warnings
- **Retry warnings**: `⏳ Retrying in Ns (attempt X/Y)...`

### Root Cause

In `hermes_cli/web_server.py`, when creating the agent for WebSocket sessions, `status_callback` is not passed to `build_agent()` / `agent_init.init_agent()`. The parameter defaults to `None`, so `_emit_status()` only calls `_vprint()` which outputs to the TUI terminal, not the WebSocket.

```python
# _emit_status in run_agent.py
def _emit_status(self, message: str) -> None:
    try:
        self._vprint(f"{self.log_prefix}{message}", force=True)  # CLI only
    except Exception:
        pass
    if self.status_callback:  # None for dashboard
        try:
            self.status_callback("lifecycle", message)
        except Exception:
            pass
```

### Expected Behavior

Dashboard WebSocket clients should receive lifecycle status events so the UI can display them. This could be implemented as:

1. Register a `status_callback` that sends a new WebSocket event type (e.g., `status.update` or `agent.status`) to the connected client
2. The Dashboard frontend (`chat.html` or equivalent) listens for this event and displays it in the chat area or as a notification bar

### Suggested Event Format

```json
{
  "type": "agent.status",
  "event_type": "lifecycle" | "warn" | "info",
  "message": "⚠️ Iteration budget exhausted (45/45) — asking model to summarise",
  "timestamp": 1717350800
}
```

### Workaround

The `turn_completion_explainer` partially covers `max_iterations_reached` by appending a hint to `final_response` when the model's summary is empty or truncated. However, when the model produces a normal-length summary (which is common), the explainer doesn't trigger, leaving the user unaware the task was cut short.

### Environment

- Hermes version: latest main
- Interface: Dashboard (WebSocket via nginx reverse proxy)
- Also affects: any custom WebSocket client that doesn't register `status_callback`

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Description

The Feishu card `form` + `input` elements are not supported by the Feishu API in production environments. Sending any card containing a `<form>` tag causes the server to silently downgrade the card content to a "请升级至最新版本客户端，以查看内容" ("Please upgrade to the latest client to view the content") message.

## Impact

- `form_submit` events are **never triggered** — the Gateway's `form_value` extraction code at `gateway/platforms/feishu.py:2822-2824` is dead code
- The `<input>` fields never render
- The submit button with `action_type: "form_submit"` becomes non-functional
- This affects all environments running against this Feishu API version/tenant configuration

## Evidence

Tested with both card JSON v1.0 (elements at root) and v2.0 (elements under body), with and without `"schema": "2.0"`. All variants produce the same downgraded result:

Server-rendered content was:


## Gateway code that handles form_value (currently unreachable)

```python
# feishu.py line 2822-2824
form_value = getattr(action, "form_value", None)
if form_value:
    action_value["_form"] = form_value
```

## Recommendation

1. Either remove or gate-keep the `form_value` extraction code since it cannot be triggered
2. Update documentation to mark form+input as unsupported
3. Alternative: investigate if a different Feishu API endpoint or template version supports form inputs

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: main branch
- Feishu API: lark-oapi SDK via WebSocket
- Feishu tenant: standard (not enterprise)
- Client: Feishu desktop v7.x

items.title: video_analyze tool sends OpenAI-style video_url content block, breaks Anthropic-protocol providers (minimax/minimax-cn)
items.body:
**Hermes Agent version:** v0.15.1 (`pyproject.toml` `version = "0.15.1"`; latest is v0.15.2 as of May 29, 2026)

**Affected tool:** `video_analyze` (registered in `tools/vision_tools.py:1253`, enabled via `hermes tools enable video` / `toolsets.py:119`)

**Affected providers:** Any provider that terminates at an Anthropic-protocol endpoint, including the officially registered `minimax` and `minimax-cn` providers (declared in `hermes_cli/config.py:4970-4971`).

---

**Summary**

`video_analyze` hard-codes an OpenAI-style content block when sending the video payload to the model:

```python
# tools/vision_tools.py:1342-1347
{
    "type": "video_url",
    "video_url": {
        "url": "data:video/mp4;base64,...",
    },
}
```

This works for OpenRouter / Gemini-style providers, but the `minimax` and `minimax-cn` providers in this repo route to `https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic` (per `config.yaml` `base_url`). That endpoint speaks the Anthropic Messages API, which expects:

```python
{
    "type": "input_video",
    "source": {
        "type": "base64",
        "media_type": "video/mp4",
        "data": "<raw base64, no data: URL prefix>",
    },
}
```

When `video_analyze` is called with `provider: minimax-cn` and `model: MiniMax-M3` (a model that *does* natively support video — see MiniMax M3 release notes 2026-06-01: "原生多模态…支持图片和视频的输入"), the request is rejected at the API with `unknown content type: video_url` (or equivalent 400).

Net effect: **users on the officially-shipped `minimax` / `minimax-cn` providers cannot use the `video_analyze` tool at all**, even though the underlying model is video-capable. The error handler at `vision_tools.py:1404-1417` then fires the "does not support video" branch and suggests `google/gemini-2.5-flash` — misleading, since the model *does* support video, the wire format is wrong.

---

**Repro**

1. Configure `minimax-cn` in `config.yaml`:
   ```yaml
   model:
     default: MiniMax-M3
     provider: minimax-cn
     base_url: https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic
   ```
2. Set `MINIMAX_CN_API_KEY` in `.env`.
3. `hermes tools enable video`
4. Add to `.env`:
   ```
   AUXILIARY_VIDEO_MODEL=MiniMax-M3
   ```
5. Start the CLI and call:
   ```
   Analyze the video at C:/Users/Admin/sample.mp4 — what is happening in it?
   ```
6. Observe: request fails before reaching the model.

---

**Suggested fix**

Make content-block construction in `video_analyze_tool` (`tools/vision_tools.py:1334-1350`) provider-aware:

- Detect current provider from `load_config()` / `os.environ["HERMES_PROVIDER"]`.
- For providers terminating at an Anthropic-protocol endpoint (`minimax`, `minimax-cn`, possibly `bedrock`), emit `input_video` block with raw base64 in `source.data`.
- For OpenAI / OpenRouter style providers, keep current `video_url` block unchanged — no regression for existing users.

A short provider check + `data_url.split(",", 1)[1]` for bare base64 should be enough; happy to send a PR if the maintainers confirm the routing approach.

Edge consideration: also need to confirm `model_tools.async_call_llm` actually dispatches to the right SDK per provider (Anthropic SDK for `minimax-cn`, not an OpenAI SDK shimmed at the endpoint). If the dispatch is provider-aware, the vision_tools change is the only delta; if not, the `task="vision"` path in model_tools also needs an update.

---

**Workaround for users on the affected providers (until this lands)**

None clean. `vision_analyze` (image) works because image blocks pass the Anthropic endpoint via a different code path, but images are the only thing that works. Falling back to ffmpeg frame extraction defeats the purpose of the native tool.

---

**Environment**

- OS: Windows 10 + git-bash
- Python: 3.11.14
- Install: `C:\Users\Admin\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\`
- `hermes config show`:
  ```
  Model: {'default': 'MiniMax-M3', 'provider': 'minimax-cn', 'base_url': 'https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic'}
  ```

items.title: [Bug]: /new and /clear hang/freeze the Hermes CLI process on Windows 11 (Git Bash MSYS2)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

When running `hermes` CLI in Windows 11 (Git Bash / MSYS2 / MINGW64 terminal), typing `/new` or `/clear` causes the entire CLI process to hang/freeze. The confirmation panel may appear briefly but keyboard input is not accepted, or the process freezes immediately without any visible confirmation. The only way to recover is to forcefully close the terminal.

This is a confirmed regression/timing issue: the old #30768 Windows deadlock was addressed with a `sys.platform == "win32"` fallback in `_prompt_text_input_modal`, but the `input()` based fallback still deadlocks when the terminal is in raw mode (as set by prompt_toolkit) on Git Bash/MSYS2.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On Windows 11, open Git Bash (MSYS2/MINGW64) — any terminal emulator running through mintty/MSYS2 runtime
2. Run `hermes` to start the interactive CLI (TUI mode)
3. Wait for the prompt_toolkit TUI to initialize (banner visible, composer ready)
4. Type `/new` and press Enter
5. **Observed:** Process hangs/freezes. If the confirmation panel appears, keystrokes are ignored; otherwise, the entire UI freezes immediately.
6. Same with `/clear`, and potentially `/undo`, `/reset`

## Expected Behavior

- `/new` should show a confirmation prompt, accept keyboard input (1/2/3 or Enter), and start a fresh session
- `/clear` should show the confirmation, accept input, then clear the screen and start a new session
- Keyboard input should work within 120 seconds (the timeout set on the modal)

## Actual Behavior

The process hangs completely. No keystrokes reach the application. The 120-second timeout in `response_queue.get()` never fires because the call stack deadlocks before the queue is even set up (the `input()` call never returns). Process must be killed via Task Manager or terminal forced closed.

## Affected Component

- CLI (interactive chat)

## Messaging Platform

- N/A (CLI only)

## Debug Report

```
version:          0.15.1 (2026.5.29) [70e1571d]
os:               Windows 10 AMD64 (also affects Windows 11)
python:           3.11.15
terminal:         Git Bash / MSYS2 / MINGW64 (mintty)
model:            deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash (custom provider)
profile:          default
```

## Operating System

Windows 11 (Git Bash MSYS2/MINGW64 terminal)

## Python Version

3.11.15

## Hermes Version

0.15.1 (2026.5.29)

## Root Cause Analysis

The root cause is in `cli.py` function `_prompt_text_input_modal()` (line ~7331) and its fallback `_prompt_text_input()` (line ~7287).

### Call chain for `/new`:

1. `process_command("new")` (line 8687) runs on the **process_loop daemon thread**
2. It calls `_confirm_destructive_slash("new", ...)` (line ~10550)
3. Which calls `_prompt_text_input_modal(...)` (line ~10609)
4. Since `sys.platform == "win32"` **even on Git Bash/MSYS2** (MSYS2 Python reports `"win32"`), the code takes the fallback at line 7386-7387:
   ```python
   if sys.platform == "win32":
       return self._prompt_text_input("Choice [1/2/3]: ")
   ```
5. `_prompt_text_input()` (line 7287) is called from the daemon thread. It checks:
   ```python
   in_main_thread = threading.current_thread() is threading.main_thread()
   ```
   Since we are the **daemon process_loop thread** (not main thread), it skips the `run_in_terminal` path and falls to the `else` branch at line 7328:
   ```python
   else:
       _ask()  # calls input() directly
   ```
6. `input()` is called while prompt_toolkit has **set the terminal to raw mode** (`tty.setraw()` / `tty.setcbreak()`). In raw mode, stdin is unbuffered — `input()` waits for a newline character, but the terminal never sends one because the cooked-mode line discipline is not active. **Result: `input()` blocks forever.**

### Why this is specific to Git Bash / MSYS2:

- On **native Windows Console** (PowerShell, cmd.exe, Windows Terminal with conhost), the raw mode set by prompt_toolkit does NOT interfere with `input()` in the same way because the Windows console API (`ReadConsole`/`ReadFile`) handles input differently than the MSYS2 PTY layer.
- On **Git Bash / MSYS2**, the MSYS2 runtime provides a POSIX-like PTY layer. prompt_toolkit sets this PTY to raw mode (`cfmakeraw()` / `TCSANOW` via termios), which does affect the MSYS2 runtime — `input()` which calls `fread()`/`read()` on the PTY's stdin sees raw bytes with no cooked-mode line buffering, so it waits forever for a `\n` that the terminal's line discipline never inserts.

### The same issue affects `/clear`, `/reset`, and `/undo` since they all go through the same `_confirm_destructive_slash` -> `_prompt_text_input_modal` -> `_prompt_text_input` -> `input()` path.

### The inline-skip escape hatch (/new now, /new --yes, /reset now) also does not help fully:

Looking at `_confirm_destructive_slash` (line 10583-10586):
```python
if cmd_original:
    _, _skip = self._split_destructive_skip(cmd_original)
    if _skip:
        return "once"
```

This skip happens **before** the modal, so `/new now` should bypass the confirmation and jump to `new_session()`. However, the user may not know to type `/new now`, and `/clear` has no such skip token at all — `/clear` accepts no arguments.

## Proposed Fix

The fix should ensure that on Windows (particularly MSYS2/Git Bash where `sys.platform == "win32"`), destructive slash command confirmation does not call `input()` while the terminal is in raw mode.

**Option A:** In `_confirm_destructive_slash`, when `sys.platform == "win32"`, temporarily restore terminal cooked mode before calling `input()`, then restore raw mode after:

```python
if sys.platform == "win32":
    # On Windows/MSYS2, prompt_toolkit sets the terminal to raw mode
    # which breaks input().  Try to restore cooked mode temporarily.
    try:
        import termios, tty
        fd = sys.stdin.fileno()
        old_settings = termios.tcgetattr(fd)
        tty.setcbreak(fd)  # or restore cooked: ...
    except Exception:
        pass
    result = self._prompt_text_input("Choice [1/2/3]: ")
    try:
        termios.tcsetattr(fd, termios.TCSANOW, old_settings)
    except Exception:
        pass
    return result
```

**Option B:** On `sys.platform == "win32"`, automatically treat all destructive commands as auto-approved (return `"once"`) when the shell is detected as MSYS2/Git Bash:

```python
if sys.platform == "win32":
    _cprint("  Auto-approved (Windows terminal detected).")
    return "once"
```

**Option C:** Add terminal inspection at startup to detect MSYS2 terminals and disable destructive slash confirmation by default, with a prominent startup warning.

I recommend **Option A** as it preserves the security/confirmation behavior while fixing the hang.

items.title: Desktop app sends empty model name to LLM API after v0.15.1 update

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

After updating from v0.14.0 to v0.15.1, the desktop app fails to send any messages. The root cause is that the agent sends an **empty model name** to the LLM API, which returns HTTP 400 "Param Incorrect". This causes the dashboard to crash-loop, and the Electron app shows "Timed out connecting to Hermes backend after 15000ms".

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Update hermes-agent to v0.15.1
2. Configure model in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:
   ```yaml
   model:
     provider: xiaomi
     name: mimo-v2.5-pro
     default: mimo-v2.5-pro
     model: mimo-v2.5-pro
     context_length: 1048576
   ```
3. Launch `hermes desktop --skip-build`
4. Desktop app starts, dashboard boots successfully
5. Any API call to the LLM fails with empty model

## Expected Behavior

The desktop app should resolve the model from config and pass it to the LLM API correctly.

## Actual Behavior

Desktop log shows:
```
[hermes]    🔌 Provider: xiaomi  Model: 
[hermes]    📝 Error: HTTP 400: Param Incorrect
[hermes]    📋 Details: {"code": "400", "message": "Param Incorrect", "param": "Not supported model "}
```

The `session.info` event correctly reports `"model": "mimo-v2.5-pro"`, but the actual API call uses an empty model string.

## Key Observations

1. **CLI and gateway work fine** — `hermes chat`, feishu sessions, and cron jobs all resolve the model correctly
2. **Config is correct** — `_resolve_model()` in `tui_gateway/server.py` returns `mimo-v2.5-pro` when tested directly
3. **Session ID persists** — A session with ID `e29b6755` keeps appearing across desktop restarts, even after:
   - Deleting all TUI sessions from state.db
   - Clearing Electron localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB
   - Adding `HERMES_MODEL=mimo-v2.5-pro` to `~/.hermes/.env`
4. **Dashboard crash-loop** — The empty model causes 400 errors, which crashes the agent, which restarts the dashboard, creating a loop
5. **The "Timed out" error is a symptom** — It happens because the dashboard is crash-looping, not because of a connection issue

## Workaround

None found. The desktop app is unusable in v0.15.1 with this provider/model configuration.

## Environment

- OS: macOS 26.5 (Mac ARM64)
- Hermes version: 0.15.1 (2026.5.29)
- Python: 3.11.14
- Provider: xiaomi (mimo-v2.5-pro)
- Previous working version: 0.14.0

items.title: [Bug]: TUI gateway command.dispatch doesn't handle skill bundles — deadlocks on /bundle-name

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Description

The TUI gateway's `command.dispatch` method handles skill slash commands
(via `build_skill_invocation_message`) but has no equivalent path for skill
bundles. When a user types any `/bundle-name` in TUI mode, the gateway spawns
a `slash_worker` but never sends the command through the pipe — the worker
waits forever in `pipe_read` for input that never arrives. Deadlock.

Meanwhile, the CLI path (`cli.py` → `_pending_input` queue) handles bundles
fine. The gap is specifically in `tui_gateway/server.py`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Define a skill bundle YAML (any valid bundle with one or more skills)
2. In TUI mode, type `/bundle-name test`
3. Observe: "⚡ Loading bundle: bundle-name" appears, then nothing — the agent
   never responds

**Process tree during deadlock:**

| Process | wchan | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `tui_gateway.slash_worker` | `pipe_read` | Waiting for command from gateway |
| `tui_gateway.entry` | `unix_stream_read` | Waiting on socket from frontend |
| `hermes --tui` | `do_wait` | Waiting on child process |

## Root Cause

`command.dispatch` (line 5751) handles skills at lines 5798–5820:

```python
from agent.skill_commands import (
    scan_skill_commands,
    build_skill_invocation_message,
)
cmds = scan_skill_commands()
key = f"/{name}"
if key in cmds:
    msg = build_skill_invocation_message(key, arg, ...)
    return _ok(rid, {"type": "skill", "message": msg, ...})
```

…then falls through to pending-input commands at line 5822. There's no
equivalent block for bundles. The bundle name never matches a skill, so it
falls through the entire dispatch chain and hits the generic `slash.exec`
fallback — which spawns the slash worker but sends it no input.

`skill_bundles` is already imported at line 6512 (for tab completion), so
`get_skill_bundles` and `build_bundle_invocation_message` are available —
they're just not called during dispatch.

## Proposed Fix

Mirror the skill dispatch pattern for bundles, inserted between the skill
block (line 5820) and the pending-input commands block (line 5822):

```python
    # ── Skill bundles — same pattern as skills above ──────────────────
    try:
        from agent.skill_bundles import (
            get_skill_bundles,
            build_bundle_invocation_message,
        )

        bundles = get_skill_bundles()
        key = f"/{name}"
        if key in bundles:
            result = build_bundle_invocation_message(
                key,
                arg,
                task_id=session.get("session_key", "") if session else "",
            )
            if result:
                bundle_msg, _loaded_names, _missing = result
                bundle_info = bundles[key]
                return _ok(
                    rid,
                    {
                        "type": "skill",
                        "message": bundle_msg,
                        "name": bundle_info.get("name", name),
                    },
                )
    except Exception:
        pass
```

This uses APIs already available in the file (imported at line 6512). Same
shape as the existing skill handler, checked before, checked after.

## Impact

- Users cannot invoke skill bundles from TUI mode. This is a feature parity
  gap with CLI mode where bundles work correctly.
- The workaround (local patch to `server.py`) is fragile — `hermes update`
  stashes and attempts to re-apply local modifications, but aborts the
  restore on ANY merge conflict elsewhere in the repo (#3523), silently
  dropping the bundle handler patch and breaking bundle loading until the
  user notices and re-applies.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: v0.15.x (main as of 2026-06-02)
- Mode: TUI (`hermes --tui`)

# fix(browser): scrub credentials from browser subprocess env

## Severity Assessment
### CVSS Assessment

| Metric | v3.1 | v4.0 |
|--------|------|------|
| **Score** | 6.3 / 10.0 | 6.9 / 10.0 |
| **Severity** | Medium | Medium |
| **Vector** | CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:N | CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:H/AT:N/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:L/VA:N/SC:H/SI:L/SA:N |
| **Calculator** | [CVSS v3.1 Calculator](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:N) | [CVSS v4.0 Calculator](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/4.0#CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:H/AT:N/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:L/VA:N/SC:H/SI:L/SA:N) |

### Threat Model Alignment
Hermes `SECURITY.md` section 2.3 describes credential scoping for subprocesses, and section 3.1 includes credential exfiltration when credentials cross a lower-trust boundary. This is a credential-exfiltration candidate because the local browser tool launches the agent-browser subprocess from the agent process environment without applying the sibling subprocess env scrubbers.

## Impact
`agent-browser` can inherit provider credentials, gateway tokens, GitHub tokens, and other operator credentials from the Hermes Python process. A compromised agent-browser binary, daemon, or browser-control path can read those variables directly instead of depending on an LLM output leak.

## Affected Component
**File:** `tools/browser_tool.py:858-914`

```python
    task_socket_dir = os.path.join(_socket_safe_tmpdir(), f"agent-browser-{tmp_session}")
    os.makedirs(task_socket_dir, mode=0o700, exist_ok=True)
    browser_env = {**os.environ, "AGENT_BROWSER_SOCKET_DIR": task_socket_dir}
    browser_env["PATH"] = _merge_browser_path(browser_env.get("PATH", ""))

    if "AGENT_BROWSER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS" not in browser_env:
        browser_env["AGENT_BROWSER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS"] = str(BROWSER_SESSION_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT * 1000)

    def _run_tmp(cmd: str, cmd_args: List[str]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        full = base_args + [cmd] + cmd_args
        # Use temp-file stdout/stderr pattern (same as _run_browser_command)
        # to avoid pipe hang from agent-browser daemon inheriting fds.
        stdout_path = os.path.join(task_socket_dir, f"_stdout_{cmd}")
        stderr_path = os.path.join(task_socket_dir, f"_stderr_{cmd}")
        stdout_fd = os.open(stdout_path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o600)
        stderr_fd = os.open(stderr_path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o600)
        try:
            # On Windows, launch the child in a new process group so parent
            # console Ctrl+C doesn't kill it with STATUS_CONTROL_C_EXIT
            # (0xC000013A = rc 3221225786), AND insulate its stdio + handle
            # inheritance from the parent.
            #
            # Additional Windows hardening beyond CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP:
            # * STARTF_USESTDHANDLES + explicit handles → CreateProcess hands
            #   the child ONLY our three chosen handles (DEVNULL stdin +
            #   temp-file stdout/stderr). Without this, some parents leak
            #   console handles that break downstream grandchild spawns — the
            #   agent-browser Rust binary spawns a detached daemon grandchild,
            #   and that grandchild's CreateProcess dies silently
            #   ("Daemon process exited during startup with no error output")
            #   when inherited parent handles are in a weird state. Observed
            #   in the Hermes CLI where sys.stdout and sys.stderr both report
            #   fileno=1 (stderr dup'd onto stdout at the OS level).
            # * close_fds=True → block inheritance of every other handle.
            #   (Default on POSIX; must be explicit on Windows for stdio.)
            _popen_extra: dict = {}
            if os.name == "nt":
                # CREATE_NO_WINDOW → don't attach a console (cmd.exe would
                # otherwise briefly allocate one for the .cmd shim).
                # Do NOT add CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP: on Python 3.11 Windows
                # it interacts with asyncio's ProactorEventLoop such that the
                # subprocess creation cancels the running loop task, which
                # surfaces as KeyboardInterrupt in app.run() and tears down
                # the CLI mid-turn. The agent thread's subprocess spawn
                # unwound MainThread's prompt_toolkit loop that way — see
                # diag log: "asyncio.CancelledError → KeyboardInterrupt".
                _CREATE_NO_WINDOW = 0x08000000
                _popen_extra["creationflags"] = _CREATE_NO_WINDOW
                _popen_extra["close_fds"] = True
                _si = subprocess.STARTUPINFO()
                _si.dwFlags |= subprocess.STARTF_USESTDHANDLES
                _popen_extra["startupinfo"] = _si
            proc = subprocess.Popen(
                full, stdout=stdout_fd, stderr=stderr_fd,
                stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, env=browser_env,
                **_popen_extra,
```

## Technical Reproduction
1. Use Hermes Agent latest upstream `main` at source receipt commit `b28dd3417dbf82f3df523dc180e59e0d154ca93a`.
2. Launch Hermes with a credential-bearing environment variable representing a provider credential, GitHub credential, or gateway bot credential.
3. Invoke any local browser tool path that reaches `_run_browser_command()`, or force the Chrome-fallback `_run_tmp()` path.
4. Inspect the `env` passed to `subprocess.Popen()` and observe it starts from `{**os.environ}` before adding browser-specific variables.
5. Expected result: the browser daemon receives only safe baseline variables plus explicit operator passthroughs, matching the other Hermes subprocess launchers.

## Demonstrated Impact
- The primary agent-browser launch path copies the full parent environment at `tools/browser_tool.py:1994`.
- The Chrome-fallback path copies the full parent environment at `tools/browser_tool.py:860`.
- Sibling launchers use env filtering (`_scrub_child_env`, `_sanitize_subprocess_env`, or `_build_safe_env`) but browser_tool does not.
- Existing browser secret tests cover URL/snapshot output leakage, not subprocess environment inheritance.

## Environment
Hermes latest-main source receipt: `b28dd3417dbf82f3df523dc180e59e0d154ca93a` on current `main`. Runtime prerequisite: local browser tool mode using `agent-browser`; whole-process wrapping may reduce exposure. Current-turn operator approval allows full public disclosure. No secrets, tokens, private logs, unrelated local paths, personal identity material, or provider transcript excerpts are included. Public submission must use the `public_security_full_disclosure` route.
Source freshness receipt: `source_ready` for `upstream-main` at `b28dd3417dbf82f3df523dc180e59e0d154ca93a` via `/tmp/hermes-plan04-source-receipt.json`; affected paths exist in the prepared latest-main checkout. Candidate-specific runtime proof continues in the next one-candidate fix-submit step unless provider-free proof is already named above.

## Remediation Advice
Build `browser_env` from a scrubbed allowlist instead of parent `os.environ`, preserving only browser-required variables and explicit operator passthroughs; add a regression test that asserts provider credentials and gateway tokens are absent from the `Popen(env=...)` argument.
